# @sap-rfc/node-rfc-library

## API Contracts

<ul>
      <li>Logger

```js
// Interface for Logger. There will be no default implementation for this interface. Consumer needs to have their own implementation of Logger and pass its instance to constructor of RFCClient class. Logger is optional parameter for RFCClient class.
export interface Logger {
  log(type: "info" | "error" | "debug", message: string): void;
}
```

  </li>
   <li>Open Connection.

```js
  // The open API takes as input a set of connection parameters and returns a connection object. The connection object can then further be used to execute and commit RFCs. At the end close can be called on the connection object.
  async function open(connectionParams: RFCConnectionParameters): Promise<RFCClientConnectionHandler>;
```

  </li>

  <li>Execute RFC.

```js
  // The execute API takes the following as input.
  // rfcName: The name of the RFC you need to execute.
  // inputParams: It is of the type of the following interface InputParams: {import: {}, changing: {}, table: {}}
  // excludeParamsFromOutput : List of parameters names you want excluded from the output from the ABAP System
  // Note: Validation will happen by default. Validation includes typechecking of import parameters, filling of mandatory parameters and checking the size of the input value.
        //Ex: 1. For BAPI_PR_CREATE, the PRHEADER is an Import parameter. The client needs to pass json object for this parameter. If Json array or any primitive type values are passed then exception will be thrown.
        //Ex: 2. For BAPI_PR_CREATE, the PRITEM is a Table parameter. The client needs to pass json array for this parameter. If Json object or any primitive type values are passed then exception will be thrown.
        //Ex: 3. For BAPI_PR_CREATE, the PR_TYPE is a field in PRHEADER parameter. The client needs to pass json string for this field. If Json object, array or any primitive type values are passed then exception will be thrown. Utility API provided as part of this library can be used for converting ABAP type to JSON type.
  // It returns a JSON object, which is the result of the execution.
  async function execute(rfcName: string, input: RFCInputParams, excludeParamsFromOutput?: string[]): Promise<RFCResponse>;
```

  </li>

  <li>Get Metadata.

```js
  // The Get Metadata API takes the following as input:
  // rfcName: The name of the RFC function module for which to fetch metadata.
  // It returns a object of type RFCMetadata, the structure of which is given in the snippet below:
  async getMetadata(rfcName: string): Promise<RFCMetadata>;

  // structure of RFCMetadata
  export interface RFCMetadata {
    import: RFCParameterMetadata[],
    export: RFCParameterMetadata[],
    changing: RFCParameterMetadata[],
    table: RFCParameterMetadata[]
}

export interface RFCParameterMetadata {
    // Parameter name
    name: string;
    // The nwrfcsdk type of the parameter
    nwrfcType: string;
    // The abap type of the parameter
    abapType: string;
    // The date/time format of the parameter. The format field only contains a value if the
    //parameter type is either date or time
    format: string;
    // Parameter length in bytes in a 1-byte-per-SAP_CHAR system
    length: number;
    //  Gives the number of decimals in case of a packed number (BCD)
    decimals: number;
    // Default value as defined in SE37
    defaultValue: string;
    // Description text of the parameter as defined in SE37
    parameterText: string;
    // Specifies whether this parameter is defined as optional in SE37
    optional: boolean;
    // fields of the parameter if the parameter is a structure/object
    fields? : RFCFieldMetadata[];
    // fields of the parameter if the parameter is a table
    tableFields?: RFCFieldMetadata[]
}

export interface RFCFieldMetadata {
    // Field name
    name: string;
    // The nwrfcsdk type of the field
    nwrfcType: string;
    // The abap type of the field
    abapType: string;
    // The date/time format of the field. The format field only contains a value if the
    //field type is either date or time
    format: string;
    // Field length in bytes in a 1-byte-per-SAP_CHAR system
    length: number;
    // If the field is of type "packed number" (BCD), this member gives the number of decimals.
    decimals: number;
    // Field offset in bytes in a 1-byte-per-SAP_CHAR system
    offset: number;
    // nested fields of the field of the field is a structure/object
    fields? : RFCFieldMetadata[];
    // nested fields of the field if the field is a table
    tableFields?: RFCFieldMetadata[]
}
```

A sample of the output we get when we use the above API to get the metadata of the RFC <b>BAPI_ISUPARTNER_CREATEFROMDATA</b> is documented here : https://github.tools.sap/spa/bapi-node-library/blob/main/rfc-metadata.json 

  </li>

  <li>Commit RFC.

```js
  // Commits the RFC.
  async function commit(): void;
```

  </li>

  <li>Close Connection.

```js
  // Closes the connection. Note that if a connection is already closed, this method will simply return.
  async function close(): void;
```

  </li>

  <li>Convert ABAP Type To JsonType.

```js
  // Convert from ABAP type to equivalent JavaScriptType type
  // abapType: accepts ABAP type like c,n,i as input parameter and returns JavaScriptType types like string, number.
  async function convertToJsonType(abapType:ABAPType): JavaScriptType;
```

  </li>

</ul>

## Step by Step usage of the library in a fresh project.

<ul>
   <li>Create a folder anywhere in your file system. Call it "RFCnodelibconsumer".</li>
   <li>Open the folder in Visual Studio Code. Go to the terminal and perform npm init.</li>
   <li>Enter the details of the project. For this example you can name the project as "noderfconsumerlib". In the end a package.json file should be automatically created.</li>
   <li>Create a .npmrc in the root of your project and the following line <b>@sap-rfc:registry=https://int.repositories.cloud.sap/artifactory/api/npm/build-releases-npm/</b>. This is the internal npm repository where the Node RFC Library will be maintained.</li>
   <li>Open the package.json. Add a "dependencies" section and in it add "@sap-rfc/node-rfc-library": "^0.0.1". Perform npm install.</li>
   <li>Add a index.js file in your project directory.</li>
   <li>Add the following javascript code in the index.js

```js
import {RFCClient, RFCUtility, RFCError, NodeRFCLibraryError, RFCUtilityError, NodeRFCLibraryErrorCode, RFCErrorCode} from "@sap-rfc/node-rfc-library";
(async () => {
  //Logger is an optional parameter
  const rfcClient = new RFCClient();
  try {
    // signature: open(connectionParams): connection.
    // Result
    // connectionObject: Object representing the connection to the backend system.
    const connection = await rfcClient.open({
      ashost: "ldciq43.wdf.sap.corp", //please provide your own test system
      sysnr: "36",
      client: "002",
      lang: "EN",
      user: "your-dlm-username",
      passwd: "your-dlm-password",
      connectivity_proxy_host: "testConnectivityHost",
      connectivity_proxy_port: "4500",
      connectivity_subaccount: "yoursubaccount",
      connectivity_proxy_authentication: "Bearer testToken",
      // TECHNICAL_USER_TOKEN: This can be given if SSO is needed in BTP. If you give this please dont provide username and password.
      // business_user_token:  This can be given if Principal propagation SSO is needed.
    });

    // execute(rfcName: string, input: RFCInputParams, enableValidation: boolean ,excludeParamsFromOutput?: string[]): {}
    // Input:
    // RFCname: The name of the RFC you need to execute.
    // inputParams: It is of the type of the following interface InputParams: {import: {}, changing: {}, table: {}}
    // enableValidation : If set to true, before executing the RFC mandatory parameter validation and datatype of Parameters and fields are validated. Note: This validation will happen inside Node RFC Library not inside SAP system.
    // excludeParamsFromOutput: List of parameters names you want excluded from the output from the ABAP System.
    // Output:
    // executionResult: A javascript object representing the output from the ABAP System.
    const executionResult = await connection.execute(
      "BAPI_PR_CREATE",
      {
        import: {
          PRHEADER: {
            PR_TYPE: "RB",
          },
          PRHEADERX: {
            PR_TYPE: "X",
          },
        },
        changing: {},
        table: {
          PRITEMX: [
            {
              PLANT: "X",
              PREQ_ITEM: "00010",
              QUANTITY: "X",
              MATERIAL: "X",
            },
          ],
          PRITEM: [
            {
              PLANT: "AAHS",
              PREQ_ITEM: "00010",
              QUANTITY: "2",
              MATERIAL: "AAH_BRAKE_1_TIER",
            },
          ],
        },
      },
      true,
      ["PLANT"]
    );

    // commit(): void
    await connection.commit();

    const metadata = await connection.getMetadata("BAPI_PR_CREATE");

    // close(): void
    await connection.close();
    // Convert ABAP Type to Javascript Type
    const javascriptType = RFCUtility.convertAbapTypeToJavaScriptType("p"); //Javascript : 'string'
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof RFCError) {
      if (error.code === RFCErrorCode.RFC_LOGON_FAILURE) {
        console.log("Logon Failure" + error.message);
      }
    } else if (error instanceof RFCUtilityError) {
      console.log("error from utility" + error.message);
    } else if (error instanceof NodeRFCLibraryError) {
      if (error.code === NodeRFCLibraryErrorCode.UNKNOW_ERROR)
        console.log("error from node rfc library" + error.message);
    }
    console.log(error);
  }
})();
```

</li>
<li>Go back to the terminal and run "node index.js".</li>
</ul>

## Usage of the library with JS Bundlers like Webpack

<li>When someone does an npm install of the @sap-rfc/node-rfc-library in a project lets say <b>YOUR_PROJECT</b>, the library would be installed in the node_modules folder. The path would typically be <b>YOUR_PROJECT/node_modules/@sap-rfc/node-rfc-library</b></li>
<li>You would find a <b>dist</b> folder in <b>YOUR_PROJECT/node_modules/@sap-rfc/node-rfc-library</b>. The dist folder has the bundle.js and also a folder called <b>sapnoderfcaddons</b></li>
<li>The <b>sapnoderfcaddons</b> contains the node addon executable and nwrfcsdk dependencies required by this lib to work.</li>
<li>When a consumer, uses this library and does not use a javascript bundler, everything works fine.</li>
<li>When a javascript bundler like webpack is used, all the JS code of all the dependencies of the consumer would be merged into a single file usually in the consumer's dist folder.</li>
<li>In this case the javascript code of @sap-rfc/node-rfc-library would also be bundled into the final output, whereas the non-JS dependencies such as the node addon executable and nwrfcsdk dependencies would be left out.</li>
<li>As of today, we could not find a solution which could bundle the executables and dlls along with Javascript. Hence it is the consumer's repsonsibility to copy the <b>sapnoderfcaddons</b> folder to the exact location where their output bundle is created.</li>
<li>If the consumer uses Webpack, this could done with a copy-webpack-plugin added as dev dependency and similar plugin configuration as shown below:

```js
const config = {
    entry: './src/index.ts',
    target: "node",
    module: {
        rules: [
            {
                test: /\.tsx?$/,
                use: "ts-loader",
                exclude: /node_modules/,
            }
        ],
    },
    devtool: "source-map",
    resolve: {
        extensions: [".ts", ".js"],
    },
    plugins: [
        new CopyPlugin({
          patterns: [
            {
              from: path.resolve(__dirname, "./node_modules/@sap-rfc/node-rfc-library/dist/sapnoderfcaddons/prebuilds"),
              to: path.resolve(__dirname, "./dist/sapnoderfcaddons/prebuilds"),
              force: true,
            },
            {
              from: path.resolve(__dirname, "./node_modules/@sap-rfc/node-rfc-library/dist/sapnoderfcaddons/nwrfcsdk"),
              to: path.resolve(__dirname, "./dist/sapnoderfcaddons/nwrfcsdk"),
              force: true,
            },
          ],
        }),
      ],
  };
}
```

</li>


## Logger

<ul>
<li>Implementation provided by consumer

```js
export class CAPLogger extends Logger {
  log(type: "info" | "error" | "debug", message: string): void {
    //Logger Implementation
  }
}
```

</li>
<li> Usage of Logger(provided by consumer) inside the RFC Library

```js
class RFCClient {
  private logger?: Logger = undefined;
  //accepts logger object passed by consumer
  constructor(logger?: Logger) {
     this.logger = logger;
  }

  async function open(connectionParams: RFCConnectionParameters): Promise<RFCClientConnectionHandler> {

      try {
	   // open connection implementation
	   logger.log("info","Calling nwrfcsdk for open connection");
	   //...

	  } catch(e) {
	    logger.log("error",e.message);
	  }
  }
}
```

</li>
</ul>

## Error Handling and Categorization

<ul>

<li>RFC Error. This error is thrown when something goes wrong during rfc call to SAP system.

```js
class RFCError {
  code: RFCErrorCode;
  group: RFCErrorGroup;
  key: string;
  message: string;
}
```

```js

enum RFCErrorCode {
  RFC_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE = 1, ///< Error in Network & Communication layer
  RFC_LOGON_FAILURE, ///< Unable to logon to SAP system. Invalid password, user locked, etc.
  RFC_ABAP_RUNTIME_FAILURE, ///< SAP system runtime error (SYSTEM_FAILURE): Shortdump on the backend side
  RFC_ABAP_MESSAGE, ///< The called function module raised an E-, A- or X-Message
  RFC_ABAP_EXCEPTION, ///< The called function module raised an Exception (RAISE or MESSAGE ... RAISING)
  RFC_CLOSED, ///< Connection closed by the other side
  RFC_CANCELED, ///< No longer used
  RFC_TIMEOUT, ///< Time out
  RFC_MEMORY_INSUFFICIENT, ///< Memory insufficient
  RFC_VERSION_MISMATCH, ///< Version mismatch
  RFC_INVALID_PROTOCOL, ///< The received data has an unsupported format
  RFC_SERIALIZATION_FAILURE, ///< A problem while serializing or deserializing RFM parameters
  RFC_INVALID_HANDLE, ///< An invalid handle was passed to an API call
  RFC_RETRY, ///< RfcListenAndDispatch did not receive an RFC request during the timeout period
  RFC_EXTERNAL_FAILURE, ///< Error in external custom code. (E.g. in the function handlers or tRFC handlers.) Results in SYSTEM_FAILURE
  RFC_EXECUTED, ///< Inbound tRFC Call already executed (needs to be returned from RFC_ON_CHECK_TRANSACTION in case the TID is already known and successfully processed before.)
  RFC_NOT_FOUND, ///< Function or structure definition not found (Metadata API)
  RFC_NOT_SUPPORTED, ///< The operation is not supported on that handle
  RFC_ILLEGAL_STATE, ///< The operation is not supported on that handle at the current point of time (e.g. trying a callback on a server handle, while not in a call)
  RFC_INVALID_PARAMETER, ///< An invalid parameter was passed to an API call, (e.g. invalid name, type or length)
  RFC_CODEPAGE_CONVERSION_FAILURE, ///< Codepage conversion error
  RFC_CONVERSION_FAILURE, ///< Error while converting a parameter to the correct data type
  RFC_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, ///< The given buffer was to small to hold the entire parameter. Data has been truncated.
  RFC_TABLE_MOVE_BOF, ///< Trying to move the current position before the first row of the table
  RFC_TABLE_MOVE_EOF, ///< Trying to move the current position after the last row of the table
  RFC_START_SAPGUI_FAILURE, ///< Failed to start and attach SAPGUI to the RFC connection
  RFC_ABAP_CLASS_EXCEPTION, ///< The called function module raised a class based exception
  RFC_UNKNOWN_ERROR, ///< "Something" went wrong, but I don't know what...
  RFC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILURE, ///< Authorization check error
  RFC_AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE, ///< The authentication handler (RFC_ON_AUTHENTICATION_CHECK) failed to authenticate the user trying to log on
  RFC_CRYPTOLIB_FAILURE, ///< Error when dealing with functions provided by the cryptolibrary
  RFC_IO_FAILURE, ///< Error when dealing with io functions, streams etc
  RFC_LOCKING_FAILURE, ///< Requesting or freeing critical sections or mutex failed
  _RFC_RC_max_value, ///< Don't use
}
```

```js
enum RFCErrorGroup {
  ABAP_APPLICATION_FAILURE = 1, ///< ABAP Exception raised in ABAP function modules
  ABAP_RUNTIME_FAILURE, ///< ABAP Message raised in ABAP function modules or in ABAP runtime of the backend (e.g Kernel)
  LOGON_FAILURE, ///< Error message raised when logon fails
  COMMUNICATION_FAILURE, ///< Problems with the network connection (or backend broke down and killed the connection)
  EXTERNAL_RUNTIME_FAILURE, ///< Problems in the RFC runtime of the external program (i.e "this" library)
  EXTERNAL_APPLICATION_FAILURE, ///< Problems in the external program (e.g in the external server implementation)
  EXTERNAL_AUTHORIZATION_FAILURE, ///< Problems raised in the authorization check handler provided by the external server implementation
  EXTERNAL_AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE, ///< Problems raised by the authentication handler (RFC_ON_AUTHENTICATION_CHECK)
  CRYPTOLIB_FAILURE, ///< Problems when dealing with functions provided by the cryptolibrary
  LOCKING_FAILURE,
}

```

</li>

<li>Utility Error.  This error is thrown if unsupported abap type passed to convertAbapTypeToJavaScriptType

```js
class RFCUtilityError {
  message: string;
}
```

</li>

<li>Node RFC Library Error. This error is thrown in cases of any internal issue in library or any explicit exception thrown from library

```js
class NodeRFCLibraryError {
  code: NodeRFCLibraryErrorCode;
  message: string;
}
```
```js
enum NodeRFCLibraryErrorCode {
  UNKNOW_ERROR,
  EMPTY_CONNECTIONPARAM,
  INVALID_CONNECTION_PARAM_KEY,
  INVALID_CONNECTION_PARAM_VALUE,
  CONNECTION_CLOSED,
  FAILED_TO_LOAD_DEPENDENCY,
  UNSUPPORTED_FIELD_DATATYPE,
  FAILED_TO_EXCLUDE_PARAMETER,
  INVALID_FIELD_VALUE,
  INPUT_PARAMETER_VALIDATION_FAILED
}
```

</li>

</ul>


## Decisions

<ul>
  <li>The execute API will take an optional parameter to do validation. If this option is set to true, then the Node RFC Library will perform validation based on the metadata. The validation includes input typechecking, input restriction checking (minLength, maxLength etc), mandatory parameter validation etc. This is not done by default because doing validation can potentially slow down performance.</li>
  <li>An utility shall be provided in the Node RFC Library to provide a mapping between ABAP Types and Javascript Types.</li>
  <li>An interface for logger shall be provided by the Node RFC Library.

```js
export interface Logger {
  log(type: "info" | "error" | "debug", message: string): void;
}
```

  </li>

</ul>

## NWRFCSDK Tracing

There are a couple of ways we can enable tracing in the NWRFCSDK. A detailed trace for a simple RFC execution (PR_CREATE) for one time is around <b>2MB</b>. This could potentially overwhelm the space in a BTP container in more complex scenarios. As a result of this, we will not be exposing any mechanism to enable the NWRFCSDK tracing as of now from the Node RFC Library. We will take it up as a requirement comes and then think about how to enable them.

## Utility

<ul>
 <li>Convert from abap type to Javascript type

The supported Abap types are being refered from the NWRFCSDK documentation [Page 8] https://support.sap.com/content/dam/support/en_us/library/ssp/products/connectors/nwrfcsdk/NW_RFC_750_ProgrammingGuide.pdf

Reference Table for mapped Javascript type to the Abap Type

| Abap Type Name | Abap Type | Javascript Type |
| -------------- | --------- | --------------- |
| Char           | c         | String          |
| Number         | n         | String          |
| Byte           | x         | Buffer          |
| BCD            | p         | String          |
| Int 4          | i         | Number          |
| Int 1          | b         | Number          |
| Int 2          | s         | Number          |
| Int 8          | 8         | BigInt          |
| FLoat          | f         | String          |
| Date           | d         | String          |
| Time           | t         | String          |
| Decf16         | a         | String          |
| Decf34         | e         | String          |
| Variable Char  | g         | String          |
| Variable Byte  | y         | Buffer          |
| UtcLong        | p         | BigInt          |

  </li>
</ul>

## Note on Connection Parameters

The following connection parameters are exposed by the BAPI Node Library:

<ul>
  <li><b>user</b>: Username</li>
  <li><b>passwd</b>: password</li>
  <li><b>ashost</b>: Hostname of the application server.</li>
  <li><b>sysnr</b>: The backend's system number. (E.g. "01").</li>
  <li><b>client</b>: The Client or "Mandant" to which to logon.</li>
  <li><b>lang</b>: Logon Language. Either specify the two-character ISO-Code (like EN for English,
			KO for Korean) or the one-character SAP-specific code (like E for English,
			3 for Korean). Note that the ISO-codes are case-insensitiv, while the SAP
			codes are not! So 'D' logs you on in German, while 'd' logs you on in
			Serbian, if that language is installed in your system.</li>
  <li><b>sysid</b>: The backend's system ID. (E.g. "H9C"). If this parameter is not specified, the value of DEST is used instead.</li>
  <li><b>snc_mode</b>: Specifies whether SNC should be activated for this connection or not. One of the following values:0 SNC off or 1 SNC on</li>
  <li><b>snc_partnername</b>: Token/identifier representing the backend system.</li>
  <li><b>mshost</b>: Hostname of the message server, which is doing the loadbalancing.</li>
  <li><b>msserv</b>: Not needed in most cases. Specify this parameter only, if the
	message server does not listen on the standard service "sapms<SysID>",
	or if this service is not defined in the services file and you need to
    specify the network port directly. Note: on Unix the services are
	defined in /etc/services, while on Windows they are defined in
	C:\WINDOWS\system32\drivers\etc\services.</li>
  <li><b>group</b>: The logon group from which the application server should be chosen. If this parameter is not specified, "PUBLIC" is used.</li>
  <li><b>saprouter</b>: If the connection needs to be made through a firewall via a SAPRouter, specify the SAPRouter parameters in the following format: /H/hostname/S/portnumber.</li>
  <li><b>connectivity_proxy_host</b>: Hostname of the Connectivity Agent</li>
  <li><b>connectivity_proxy_port</b>: Port number or service string of the Connectivity Agent's listening port</li>
  <li><b>connectivity_subaccount</b>: Subaccount inside the cloud environment</li>
  <li><b>connectivity_proxy_authentication</b>: Optionally, authentication token to authenticate at the Connectivity Agent.
     Prior to the token the authformat has to be specified in the form <authformat> <token>. For example Bearer <base64-encoded-token></li>
  <li><b>connectivity_location_id</b>: Optionally, Location ID as identifier for the SAP Cloud Connector</li>
  <li><b>technical_user_token</b>: Optionally, Technical User SSO Token to propagate to the SAP Cloud Connector</li>
  <li><b>business_user_token</b>: Optionally, Principal propagation SSO Token of the business user to propagate to the SAP Cloud Connector</li>
</ul>
